Multinucleation (frac_large_nucleus z up to 61, multinucleate_proxy z up to 18.7) plus flat frac_mitotic_like should have pointed to replication/DNA-damage rather than primary tubulin targeting. Literature supports: mitoxantrone-topo II alpha interaction (PMID 27834128), topo II inhibition and DNA-damage signaling to replication after mitoxantrone (PMID 22140093), topo II mechanism review (PMID 42442624), replication fork arrest at topo II cleavage sites (PMID 9153414).

reflection.text:
I called Microtubule stabilizers at 0.60 and was wrong; unblinding showed mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II-alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor, and the protocol NSC majority vote of 2/4 wells for DNA replication was correct. The true mechanism is consistent with mitoxantrone interaction with topoisomerase II-alpha (PMID 27834128) and with DNA damage signaling linked to replication after mitoxantrone (PMID 22140093).

What misled me was tubulin texture: tub_glcm_contrast rho=+1.00 (e13) and tub_std rho=+1.00 (e18) plus high z-scores for tub_glcm_contrast, cell rounding, and large irregular nuclei in e2, e3 and e9, combined with k-neighbour 6/10 then 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers in e6/e10 and microscopist candidate Microtubule stabilizers in e5. I treated monotonic tubulin contrast/bundling and rounding as primary stabilization, when it was secondary cytoskeletal collapse downstream of topoisomerase II-mediated replication arrest (PMID 9153414) and topoisomerase II disruption of replication (PMID 42442624).

What I underweighted was the decisive comparison: per-well NSC votes for DNA replication at 0.3 uM and 10 uM in the verdict tally, which I dismissed as a low-similarity split, and the negative controls e12 frac_multinucleate_proxy rho=-0.20 and e16 frac_mitotic_like constant that argued against Aurora/Eg5 and mitotic-arrest stabilization. My acquisition choice made this worse by spending all 4 wells on singletons at 0.3, 1, 3 and 10 uM including the 6-cell 10 uM well e3, leaving no replicate to satisfy the review request for 1 uM rep2 phospho-H3/mitotic testing.

Over-interpreted high-dose morphology in 6-cell well e3 and e5 rounding/tubulin clumping as stabilizer bundles while discounting toxicity-driven collapse.
Dismissed NSC 2/4 DNA replication vote as low-sim split and kept DNA replication at 0.10 in e14/e19 despite it being the protocol winner.

## Reflection

I called Microtubule stabilizers at 0.60 and was wrong; unblinding showed mitoxantrone, a DNA topoisomerase II-alpha inhibitor and DNA inhibitor, and the protocol NSC majority vote of 2/4 wells for DNA replication was correct. - Overweighted k-neighbour 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers in e10 and monotonic tub_glcm_contrast and tub_std in e13/e18 as direct stabilization instead of secondary effects of replication stress.
- Over-interpreted high-dose morphology in 6-cell well e3 and e5 rounding/tubulin clumping as stabilizer bundles while discounting toxicity-driven collapse.

- Spent budget on four singleton doses with no replicate, so could not acquire requested 1 uM rep2 to independently test mitotic arrest.
